rq: joint identification of raw language equivalence and latent intervention partition
primary_work: Lin et al., Learning to Model the World With Language, ICML 2024 Oral
decision: NARROWED BEYOND FUTURE-PREDICTIVE MULTIMODAL LANGUAGE WORLD MODELS — NOT ADOPTED
reason: Dynalang establishes language-conditioned multimodal future prediction, imagined-rollout control, and text-only pretraining as empirical prior art. These results are functional rather than a theorem jointly identifying raw-language equivalence, latent intervention-target blocks, and denotation. Predictive-equivalent targets admit different semantic refinements; simultaneous utterance/target/latent/world-interface recoding preserves the complete predictive and interactive law; and text-only pretraining cannot choose the external denotation map.
surviving_candidate: After recovering the finest raw-language equivalence supported by legitimate language dynamics, the finest target partition supported by non-language interventions, and the strongest future-predictive multimodal alignment obtainable from Dynalang-like world modeling, determine whether a preregistered cross-system intervention uniquely separates only the remaining predictive-, policy-, and reward-aliased classes while eliminating every utterance/target/latent/world-interface recoding preserving the complete language, observation, transition, reward, and action laws.
public_baseline_reproduction: not started; official code and exact commit are available, but a minimal task subset, exact commands, external dependency and asset pins, three seeds, resource limits, model-byte/RSS/time measurement, artifact checksums, and direct Q/P/d metrics must be preregistered first
